answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock $100 for a 30-day horizon before it can bid on jobs, whether composing a sonnet or pricing quartz. Each identity gets the same bid limit, so splitting into 1,000 aliases requires $100,000 locked for a month. The rule does not prove identities are unique; it makes multiplying them consume capital, denying an attacker cheap extra bidding capacity while tying up funds.
